title: Private Deployments: VPC & On‑Prem Reference, Day-2 Ops, Upgrades, and Customer Requirements
author: Aisha Raman
body:
Overview

This document is a consolidated reference for Redwood Inference private deployments. It covers VPC-based cloud deployments, reference architectures for common customer topologies, the on-prem packaging and installation checklist, day-1 operational procedures (monitoring, backups, scaling), and step-by-step upgrade & rollback procedures. It also contains a customer requirements library that teams can use to drive scoping and presales work.

Audience: Platform/solutions engineers, customer SREs, implementation engineers, sales engineers, and SOC/compliance reviewers.

Goals
- Provide a single source-of-truth for private deployment patterns and expectations.
- Reduce onboarding time for implementation and support teams.
- Standardize upgrade and rollback processes to minimize customer-impact windows.
- Capture common customer requirements so proposals/quotations are consistent.

Owners & Contacts
- Primary owner: eng-platform (private-deployments squad)
- On-call: private-deployments rotations (see runbooks)
- Escalation: Platform Pager + Solutions Eng Slack #private-deployments

1) Deployment modes & when to use them
- Hosted VPC (recommended for most cloud customers): Redwood control plane managed; customer provides VPC & peering/private link. Best for customers who need network isolation but want Redwood to manage infra.
- Dedicated VPC (reserved capacity): For customers requiring dedicated GPU capacity with contractual throughput guarantees.
- Private (customer-managed control plane / on-prem): For regulated or air-gapped environments. Customer owns cluster, network, and key management.

2) VPC Deployment Guide (cloud)
Intro: Typical deployment for AWS/GCP/Azure. This section focuses on AWS examples; equivalents for GCP/Azure are included in linked templates.

Prerequisites
- Customer cloud account and admin contact
- CIDR allocation for Redwood subnets (non-overlapping with customer on-prem if VPN used)
- KMS key or HSM access for key material (if requested)
- Service account / IAM role for Redwood deployment automation

Network & Security configuration (recommended defaults)
- VPC: single tenant VPC owned by customer
- Subnet layout: 3 AZs, public NAT subnets (for egress), private worker subnets per AZ
- CIDR examples: 10.40.0.0/16 (VPC), private worker subnets 10.40.1.0/24, 10.40.2.0/24, 10.40.3.0/24
- Security groups:
  - SG-Worker: Allow inbound from SG-API (TCP 5100-5200), ephemeral ports for health checks; outbound 0.0.0.0/0 for container pulls (or restrict to your registry CIDR)
  - SG-API: Allow inbound from customer network (CIDR) and Redwood control plane IPs; allow 443/8443 for public API endpoint (if exposed)
- NACLs: stateless filters apply; prefer SG for L7/L4 controls and keep NACL permissive unless required by policy

IAM / Roles
- Role: Redwood-Deployment-Manager (assume-role for automation)
- Minimum policy snippets (example):
  - eks:CreateCluster, iam:PassRole (for worker nodes), ec2:CreateSecurityGroup, ec2:DescribeSubnets
  - s3:GetObject for downloading images/config artifacts
(Include complete policy JSON in the deployment artifact repository)

Data plane storage & artifacts
- EBS vs NVMe: Worker volumes should use NVMe/instance-store for low-latency KV caches; EBS gp3 for persistent model store and container layering.
- S3 buckets: encrypted with customer KMS, with prefix/redwood-artifacts/ and lifecycle rules (30-day warm, 365-day cold).

Example network diagram (text)
- Customer VPC
  - Public subnets (NAT GW)
  - Private subnets (worker nodes)
  - PrivateLink endpoint to Redwood control plane (optional)
  - Transit Gateway / VPN to on-prem (when hybrid)

3) Reference architectures (common topologies)
- Small dev/proof-of-concept (1 AZ, 2 worker nodes, single model replica)
- Production high-availability (3 AZ, autoscaling node groups, model replication across zones, multi-node KV caching)
- Regulated environment (private control plane, HSM-backed KMS, egress-restricted worker nodes, no public endpoints)
- Hybrid (on-prem inference for sensitive data + cloud for non-sensitive batch workloads)

Architecture checklist (table style, single-line items separated by semicolons)
- HA: 3 AZs; autoscaling; cross-zone load balancer; health checks; replication across AZs
- Security: KMS/HSM; VPC endpoints only; private link for control-plane; RBAC enforced; audit logging to centralized SIEM
- Observability: Prometheus metrics, Grafana dashboards, distributed tracing and per-route token cost logs
- Backups: regular model/object store snapshots; model artifact versioning; DB backups (etcd/postgres)

4) On-prem packaging & installation checklist
Supported platforms and prerequisites
- Supported OS: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (preferred), RHEL 8.6+ (enterprise support), RKE2/K3s for air-gapped minimal installs
- Container runtime: containerd 1.6+; CRI-O supported with validation
- Kubernetes: 1.26-1.28 (tested matrix) – consult release notes for compatibility
- Minimum hardware profiles:
  - Control plane nodes (if customer operates control plane): 4 vCPU, 16GB RAM, 100GB SSD (x3 for HA)
  - Worker nodes (inference): GPU nodes – common configs: A100(40GB)/H100 or equivalent; CPU-only inference supported for small models

Packaging contents (artifact names)
- redwood-private-release-2026-<version>.tar.gz (contains helm charts, CRDs, manifests)
- images.txt (SHASUM file mapping image names to digests)
- offline-registry.tar (optional for air-gapped installs)
- installation-runbook.md

Installation steps (high-level)
1. Validate hardware and networking; ensure NTP and DNS are operational.
2. Unpack release artifacts on bastion / install host.
3. Load images to local registry (air-gapped) or configure imagePullSecrets.
4. Apply CRDs and core services via helm: redwood-core -> redwood-runtime -> redwood-operator.
5. Validate health: kubectl wait --for=condition=Available deployment/redwood-core --namespace redwood-system --timeout=10m
6. Register cluster with Redwood control plane (for private-managed installs) or configure local-only mode.

Package verification checklist
- All CRDs installed; operator in Running state; image digests match images.txt; TLS certs valid and signed by approved CA; audit logs streaming to customer SIEM.

5) Day-1 operations (maintenance & runbooks)
Monitoring & alerting (SLO-driven)
- Core SLOs: 99.95% P90 availability for API endpoints; P95 token latency < 250ms for small-model baseline; queue length thresholds < 100 requests.
- Key alerts: node GPU saturation (>80% sustained), model replica OOM, KV cache hit rate drop (>10% below baseline), control-plane API error rate spike (>1% 5m window).
- Dashboards: per-customer per-model latency, per-route cost, token breakdown, GPU utilization heatmap.

Logging & tracing
- Logs: structured JSON; ship to centralized ELK/Datadog; include request_id, route_id, model_version, token_count.
- Tracing: OpenTelemetry spans for request lifecycle including coldstart, KV cache lookup, model inference time.

Scaling & capacity management
- Horizontal autoscaling: recommend HPA + custom metrics (pending request queue length, model-load average).
- Scheduled scaling: predictable morning traffic, reserve burstable nodes for batched workloads.
- Capacity runbooks: pre-warm model replicas before major marketing events; load-test ahead of SLA ramp.

Backups and recovery
- Model artifact snapshot cadence: daily for active models; weekly full snapshots.
- Config DB (Postgres/Etcd) backups: hourly WAL archiving + daily full snapshots retained 30 days.
- Disaster recovery test plan: annual restore test with RTO target 4 hours for core control plane.

Maintenance windows & communication
- Recommended weekly maintenance window: Sunday 03:00-05:00 local time (negotiable).
- Customer notification: 7-day initial notice for planned upgrades; 48-hour reminder and 2-hour pre-notification.

6) Upgrade and rollback procedures
Principles
- Prefer in-place canary upgrades with traffic shifting; avoid large blast radius.
- Keep immutable release artifacts (images with SHA).
- Test upgrades in staging that mirrors production (same node types and model load).

Pre-upgrade checklist
- Successful snapshot of control plane and config DB; store snapshot location.
- Confirm health (all deployments Available) and baseline metrics collected for last 1 hour.
- Confirm rollback image digests are available in registry.
- Stakeholder notification completed.

Step-by-step upgrade (canary-first)
1. Move a single small percentage of traffic to canary (5-10%) after deploying new runtime pods in a separate deployment.
2. Run smoke tests: token-level functional tests, latency checks, and model quality quick evals on a representative prompt set.
3. Monitor for 15-30 minutes (depending on SLA); key checks: 5xx errors, latency spikes, model output regressions.
4. If stable, increase traffic to 25-50% for next verification window.
5. If stable at 50% for the verification window, proceed to full rollout in 10-20% increments with monitoring at each step.
6. Post-rollout: run a full regression suite and notify stakeholders.

Rollback procedure (on failure)
1. Immediately shift traffic away from canary back to previous stable deployment (automated traffic manager or manual LB rule).
2. Scale down or cordon canary pods; if stateful, ensure KV caches are safely drained.
3. Invoke rollback runbook: redeploy previous image digests to any replaced deployments and validate health.
4. Restore control plane/config DB from snapshot if data model changes occurred and are incompatible; follow restore playbook.
5. Postmortem: collect debug artifacts, tag incident, and open regression triage ticket.

7) Customer requirements library (scoping checklist)
Instructions: Use this table during discovery calls. For each item capture "Customer answer" and "Notes" in the presales form.
- Network: VPC owned by customer?; CIDR blocks required?; VPN/Direct Connect or PrivateLink?; outbound egress allowed?
- Compliance: SOC2/ISO/GDPR applicability?; data residency requirement?; encryption at rest and in transit mandated?
- Key Management: customer KMS/HSM required?; key rotation policy?; BYOK?
- Capacity: expected peak rps; average request size (tokens); concurrency; preferred GPU type; warm model replicas required?
- Connectivity: blade firewall rules; proxy/HTTP/MTLS in front of endpoints?
- Observability: log retention duration; SIEM integration (syslog/HTTPS); alert routing; SSO/SCIM integration required?
- Backup & DR: RPO/RTO expectations; offsite backups required?; restore window constraints?
- Legal/Contractual: SLA target, penalty clauses, data deletion/retention clauses.

Sample requirement template (comma separated single-line entries)
- Requirement ID: NET-001; Category: Network; Required: yes; Description: Customer requires AWS Direct Connect to Redwood control plane; Notes: provisioning lead time 6 weeks
- Requirement ID: SEC-003; Category: Keys; Required: yes; Description: Customer requires HSM-backed KMS and BYOK; Notes: customer HSM vendor: Thales

8) Operational playbooks & runbook pointers (links)
- Installation runbook: installation-runbook.md (packaged with release)
- Upgrade runbook: private-deployments-upgrade-runbook.md
- Incident runbook: private-deployments-incident-response.md
- Backup & restore: private-deployments-backup-restore.md

Appendices
A. Example IAM policy snippet (single-line placeholder)
- {"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow","Action":["eks:CreateCluster","iam:PassRole"],"Resource":"*"}]}

B. Quick troubleshooting checklist
- API 5xx errors: check control plane pods, API gateway, rate-limiter; tail logs for request_id.
- High GPU utilization: identify hot routes, scale worker pool, pre-warm model replicas.
- Model quality regression: compare outputs against golden prompt set; rollback to previous model version if severe.

C. Related artifacts and templates (packaged in release)
- Terraform module examples for VPC and EKS/GKE/AKS
- Helm charts and values.yaml examples (production and air-gapped values files)
- Prometheus alert rules and Grafana dashboards
